In an increasingly noisy and overstimulated world, a new travel trend called silence tourism is emerging, where people seek destinations that promise stillness, solitude, and an escape from digital distractions. Unlike traditional vacations focused on entertainment or sightseeing, silence tourism encourages introspection and emotional detox. Remote monasteries in Bhutan, soundproof forest cabins in Finland, and silent retreats in the Himalayas are gaining popularity among urban dwellers looking to reset mentally. This form of travel doesn't merely offer peace - it fosters a deep reconnection with one's thoughts, often leading to improved well-being. Travellers are deliberately disconnecting from smartphones and social media, choosing instead to listen to nature or their own inner voices. In a time when constant connectivity is equated with productivity, silence tourism challenges that belief by promoting mindfulness and calm as equally valuable. It turns travel into a meditative experience, revealing that silence, often overlooked, is a luxury many didn't realize they needed.

As per the passage, what is the primary purpose of silence tourism as described in the passage?

To disconnect from digital distractions and encourage introspection
To increase productivity through remote work travel
To promote group adventures in remote destinations
questions.solution_en:
The passage clearly states that silence tourism is about escaping digital distractions, embracing stillness, and encouraging introspection and emotional detox. The focus is on mindfulness, inner peace, and reconnecting with one's thoughts, rather than sightseeing or productivity. Therefore, option (b) best captures the primary purpose of silence tourism as presented in the passage.

Professionalism is probably the _____ (A) theoretical of the types of soft skills, and certainly the most dependent on context. What professionalism ______ (B) in one organization can be very different from what it means in another. In general, what most employers mean when they say they are _______ (C) for professionalism is someone who understands how they as an individual affect the ______ (D) as a whole. Select the appropriate word to fill blank A.
questions.solution_en:
The blank requires an adverb that is in Superlative degree to qualify the adjective 'theoretical' as the sentence denotes 'professionalism' is the ultimatum of the soft skills. 'Less' is in a positive degree while 'more' and 'lesser' are in comparative degrees which can be used when two objects are in comparison. Since that is not the context of the sentence, they are negated. 'Most' which means 'forming the superlative of adjectives and adverbs, especially those of more than one syllable' is the appropriate adverb in the superlative form that can qualify the adjective 'theoretical' in the context of the given sentence.

Hence, the correct answer is option (c).

Note:

Qualifiers: A word or phrase that limits the meaning of another word or phrase or makes it less general. 'Adverbs' and 'adjectives' are qualifiers.

· The Positive Degree is used to denote the mere existence of some quality of what we speak about. It is used when no comparison is made.

· The Comparative degree denotes a higher degree of quality than the positive and is used when two things are compared.

· The Superlative degree indicates the highest degree of quality and is used when more than two things (or sets of things) are compared.

Directions [Set of 4 Questions]: Read the given passage and answer the questions that follow:

King Krishnadevaraya loved horses and had a collection of some of the best breeds of horses in his stable. Once a horse trader from Arabia came to the court of Krishnadevaraya and told him that he had some very good breed of Arabian horses for sale. He invited the King to see the horse that he had brought with him and told him that if he liked it, he would send for the other horses too. The King loved the horse and told him that he would like all his horses. The King paid him 5000 gold coins as an advance, and the trader promised that he would return with the other horses in 2 days before leaving.

Two days passed by, then two weeks and still, the trader did not return. The King got more and more anxious. One evening, to relax his mind, he went to take a stroll in the garden. There he saw Tenali Raman writing down something on a paper. The King went up to him and asked what he was writing. He did not get an answer. The King further quizzed him. Tenali then looked up and told the King that he was writing down the names of the biggest fools of the Vijayanagar Kingdom.

The King took the paper from him and saw his name written at the top. He was furious with Tenali and asked for an explanation. To that, Tenali replied that any man who gives away 5000 gold coins to a total stranger is a fool. The King then asked Tenali what if he returned with the horses; to which Tenali said then, in that case, that man would be a fool. He would then write down the trader's name instead of the king's.

What was the King's reaction when he saw his name on Tenali Raman's list?
options_en: He laughed and agreed with Tenali's reasoning.
He got furious and demanded an explanation from Tenali.
He apologized to Tenali for being too trusting.
He asked Tenali to rewrite the list with more names.
questions.solution_en: The passage states, "The King took the paper from him and saw his name written at the top. He was furious with Tenali and asked for an explanation." (Paragraph 3) This demonstrates the King's anger upon discovering his name on the list, as he was offended by Tenali's judgment. Hence, (b) is the correct answer.
questions.solution_hi: The passage states, "The King took the paper from him and saw his name written at the top. He was furious with Tenali and asked for an explanation." (Paragraph 3) This demonstrates the King's anger upon discovering his name on the list, as he was offended by Tenali's judgment. Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

questions.q_en:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Long lines of cars can be _______ outside gas stations in major cities.
questions.solution_en:
We can only use a participle verb after 'be'. The use of the present participle verb (-ing form of the verb) makes the sentence active. The -ing form of the verb 'see' doesn't fit in the sentence. The subject of the sentence is 'long queues of cars'. So, the passive voice 'be seen' fits in the sentence as the sentence gives emphasis on the receiver of the action. So, the past participle form of the verb will be appropriate here.

Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

The correct sentence is: Long lines of cars can be seen outside gas stations in major cities.

Note:

Voice of a sentence - Depending upon the emphasis we want to lay we use a particular voice in a particular context. We use active voice to lay emphasis on the doer of the action while we use passive voice to lay emphasis on the receiver of the action.

Example:

Active- Radha will work. (emphasis on Radha)

Passive- Work will be done by Radha. (emphasis on Work)

Participle: A word formed from a verb (e.g. going, gone, being, been) and used as an adjective (e.g. working woman, burnt toast) or a noun (e.g. good breeding). In English, participles are also used to make compound verb forms (e.g. is going, has been). Consider the sentences given below:

Dancing at the party, the women fell on the ground.

Encouraged by her parents, Rita went on to pursue her passion.

The highlighted word in the first sentence is of the form Verb + ing and is used as a present participle. It is used to denote an action that is going on or incomplete or imperfect.

The highlighted word in the second sentence is of the form verb + ed. It is used as a past participle. It denotes the completed action or state of the thing spoken of.

A past participle ends with the following: -ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n.

One should take great care and never get confused between a gerund and a present participle. They use the same forms but perform different functions: a gerund is a verbal noun, while a present participle is a verbal adjective.

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.

The orders have been processed by the customer service team. The shipments have been dispatched by the logistics department.
options_en: The customer service team has processed the orders. The logistics department has dispatched the shipments.
The customer service team has been processing the orders. The logistics department has dispatched the shipments.
The customer service team had processed the orders. The logistics department had dispatched the shipments.
The customer service team is processing the orders. The logistics department is dispatching the shipments.
questions.solution_en:
The subject of the Passive Voice is changed into the object of the Active Voice. Also, the object of the Passive Voice is changed into the subject of the Active Voice.

The removal of the "to be" verb [been] and the preposition 'by' is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Passive to Active.

The Passive voice in the given question is in Present Perfect tense. Thus, the Active voice will also be in Present Perfect.

In Passive voice, the format is: Object of the Active voice (Subjective case) + has/have + been + V3 + by + Subject of the Active voice (Objective case).

Thus, the format of Active voice is: Subject + has/have + V3 + Object.

For example:

A new horse has been bought by Arya. (Passive Voice)

Arya has bought a new horse. (Active Voice)

The options except (a) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Active Voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is: The customer service team has processed the orders. The logistics department has dispatched the shipments.

Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

questions.q_en:
Select the word from the sentence below, which is an antonym for the word 'nebulous'.

The vague plan was rejected, so the team requested a more precise set of instructions to properly follow for the project.
questions.solution_en:
"Nebulous" means in the form of a cloud or haze; hazy, unclear, or vague. We are looking for its opposite.

a) vague - means of uncertain, indefinite, or unclear character or meaning. This is a synonym for "nebulous."

b) precise - means marked by exactness and accuracy of expression or detail. This is the direct opposite of "nebulous."

c) project - refers to the enterprise or task. It is unrelated.

d) properly - is an adverb meaning correctly or satisfactorily. It is unrelated.

Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.

questions.q_en: Describe how you will say She is painting a beautiful picture In passive voice.
options_en: A beautiful picture is painting her.
A beautiful picture is being painted by her.
She is being painted by a beautiful picture.
questions.solution_en:
The subject of the Active Voice is changed into the object of the Passive Voice. Also, the object of the Active Voice is changed into the subject of the Passive Voice.

The usage of a "to be" form of verb is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.

In Passive Voice, the preposition "by" is used before the object. However, it is optional in some cases.

The Active voice in this question is in Present Continuous. Thus, the Passive voice will also be in Present Continuous.

The format of Active voice is: Subject + am/is/are + V1 + ing + Object.

Thus, in Passive voice, the format will be: Object of the active voice (Subjective case) + am/is/are + being + V3 + by + Subject of the active voice (Objective case).

For example:

Arnab is typing a document. (Active Voice)

A document is being typed by Arnab. (Passive Voice)

The options except (b) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Passive Voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is: A beautiful picture is being painted by her.

Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.

The phrase 'ward away' is incorrect. The correct phrasal verb is 'ward off' (prevent someone or something from harming or affecting one). It is grammatically and contextually correct in this sentence. Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

Note:

Example: She has always looked down on me. Here, the phrasal verb 'to look down on someone' doesn't mean that you are looking down from a higher place at someone who is below you; it means that you think that you are better than someone.
